LESSON: TIME

Grade: PP1
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Time

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Time. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify number symbols 1-9 as 10 lessons charts for development of numeracy skills and for ordering numbers
2. arrange number cards in sequence 1-9
3. arrange number cards in sequence for completing sequence puzzles 56
4. enjoy arranging numbers in sequence in their day to day life. using ICT devices sequence from 1-9 using ICT devices in given sets of numbers using ICT devices.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify number symbols 1-9 as 10 lessons charts for development of numeracy skills and for ordering numbers

2. arrange number cards in sequence 1-9
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to arrange number cards in sequence 1-9. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. arrange number cards in sequence for completing sequence puzzles 56

4. enjoy arranging numbers in sequence in their day to day life. using ICT devices sequence from 1-9 using ICT devices in given sets of numbers using ICT devices.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

2. Explain Time to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.

4. Show that you can: identify number symbols 1-9 as 10 lessons charts for development of numeracy skills and for ordering numbers
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Time. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Time important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.
